name: Northern white rhinoceros

population.source: Save the Rhino / IUCN SSC AfRSG

note: Najin and Fatu — the last two, both female, under armed guard.

donate.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy
donate.note: houses Najin & Fatu — funds the rangers guarding the actual last two

donate.name: Save the Rhino International
donate.note: funds ranger teams and rhino recovery across Kenya

name: Western black rhinoceros
note: Declared extinct in 2011 — no confirmed sighting since 2006, none ever in captivity. What a zero looks like.

donate.name: Save the Rhino International
donate.note: too late for this one — for the ~6,800 black rhinos still here

donate.name: International Rhino Foundation
donate.note: funds ranger protection for the remaining African and Asian rhinos

name: Vaquita
note: The world's rarest marine mammal; likely fewer than a dozen remain.

donate.name: Sea Shepherd
donate.note: ships patrolling the refuge year-round — donations via this page are designated to the vaquita campaign

donate.name: Viva Vaquita
donate.note: researcher-led coalition focused entirely on the vaquita

name: Kākāpō
regions: Codfish, Anchor & Little Barrier islands, NZ
note: Every individual has a name, a transmitter and a dossier.

donate.name: NZ DOC Kākāpō Recovery
donate.note: the official programme — 100% of donations go to the Mauri Ora Kākāpō Trust

donate.name: World Parrot Trust
donate.note: supports kākāpō diet, health monitoring and release-planning work

name: Amur leopard

population.source: Land of the Leopard NP camera-trap census

note: The rarest cat on earth, back from ~30 in the 1990s.

donate.name: WildCats Conservation Alliance
donate.note: 100% of donations to field projects — their partners cover ~93% of remaining wild leopards

donate.name: Wildlife Conservation Society
donate.note: runs monitoring and protection work across the Russia–China leopard range

name: Javan rhinoceros
regions: Ujung Kulon NP, Java, Indonesia — the entire species on one peninsula

population.source: KLHK camera-trap census; disputed by Auriga Nusantara poaching report

note: Official count is ~82 — but arrests in 2024 over 26 poached rhinos suggest the real number may be far lower. We show the range, not the press release.

donate.name: International Rhino Foundation
donate.note: funds the Rhino Protection Units patrolling Ujung Kulon 15+ days a month, year-round

donate.name: Save the Rhino International
donate.note: co-funds Javan and Sumatran rhino protection programmes

name: Mountain gorilla
note: One of conservation's few genuine comebacks — up from ~680 in 2008.

donate.name: Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund
donate.note: daily tracker teams in the field since 1967

donate.name: Gorilla Doctors
donate.note: the veterinary teams that keep individual wild gorillas alive

name: California condor
note: Down to 27 in 1987 — every bird alive descends from captive breeding.

donate.name: Ventana Wildlife Society
donate.note: releases and tracks the central CA flock; lead-ammo outreach is the #1 preventable killer

donate.name: Yurok Condor Restoration Program
donate.note: indigenous-led reintroduction on Yurok ancestral territory

name: Whooping crane
regions: Wood Buffalo NP, Canada · Aransas NWR, Texas · Louisiana
note: 16 birds in 1941. ~700 wild now — the rest are the breeding stock that keeps them coming back.

donate.name: International Crane Foundation
donate.note: the crane org — runs the captive-breeding programme the recovery stands on

donate.name: Friends of the Wild Whoopers
donate.note: small 501(c)(3) securing stopover habitat along the migration corridor

name: Tiger
regions: India · Nepal · Bhutan · Bangladesh · Russia · SE Asia
note: India holds ~75% of the wild population and counts it per-state.

donate.name: Panthera
donate.note: all wild cats; overhead funded separately so gifts go to the field

donate.name: WildCats Conservation Alliance
donate.note: tigers and Amur leopards are its only two species; 100% to field projects

name: African savanna elephant
note: The best-monitored big animal on earth — the AED tracks it per survey zone.

donate.name: Save the Elephants
donate.note: WCN partner — 100% of your gift reaches STE in Kenya

donate.name: Sheldrick Wildlife Trust
donate.note: the orphan-rescue specialists — foster a calf, watch it rewild

name: Saiga antelope
note: 48,000 in 2005 → ~1.9M now. Proof the pixels can come back.

donate.name: Saiga Conservation Alliance
donate.note: the dedicated saiga org — UK charity; US donors route via WCN for tax deduction

donate.name: Altyn Dala Conservation Initiative
donate.note: the steppe restoration itself — Earthshot Prize winner, saiga as flagship
